# Oophorectomy

**Authors:** Ashli A. Lawson, Rebecca M. Rentea

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Oophorectomy is the surgical removal of one or both ovaries and may also involve the removal of the fallopian tubes. Although hysterectomy is the most common major gynecologic surgery, salpingo-oophorectomy is frequently performed in conjunction with it. Surgery for ovarian pathology is still commonly performed in females of all ages. While the removal of one ovary typically does not significantly affect the hormonal status of a patient, bilateral oophorectomy results in infertility, menopause, and associated physiological changes and risks. Thoughtful discussions with the patient are essential before proceeding with oophorectomy. The role of laparoscopy, laparotomy, and risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy will also be explored.
